positioning:
This is the lane where he is genuinely ahead of the field for his experience level. Most junior candidates have used an LLM. He has built and operated pipelines that do real work on a schedule, self-hosted a model, and shipped automation that other people's work depends on. That is a portfolio argument, not a resume-bullet argument, so lead with the repos and the systems, not with adjectives.

Most postings in this lane grade Tier A or Tier B. The honest gap is evaluation: he can build the pipeline, and he cannot yet show he measured whether it was any good. Closing that with a documented eval on one existing pipeline would be a small amount of work for a large credibility gain, and it is also the thing that makes QA lane 1 and this lane reinforce each other.
interview_watch: Expect to be asked what broke and how you found it. Pipeline work interviews well when the answer is specific about a failure: a rate limit, a malformed payload, a prompt that drifted. Have two of those ready. Expect also "how do you know the output is correct", which is the evaluation gap, so answer it honestly and say what you would put in place.
pr_note: All three codes are TEER 1, which feeds Express Entry's Canadian Experience Class cleanly. 21232 is on the North Bay RCIP list. AIP covers the lane entirely, and Ontario's Workforce Priority stream takes any of them with a qualifying offer. The entry bar for this lane stays deliberately generous because the differentiator is real.
not_required: Research-level machine learning, publications, a graduate degree in ML. A posting requiring those is a data scientist seat, not this lane.
